chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said:

I wrote to a man asking him to ask Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and he said: “The water of the well is ample; nothing spoils it unless its smell or its taste changes. Then water should be drawn from it until the smell goes away and its taste becomes good, because it has a source.”

key_terms.فَيُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out from it
key_terms.لَا يُفْسِدُهُ شَيْءٌ: nothing renders it spoiled or impure
key_terms.مَادَّةً: a replenishing source feeding the well
key_terms.وَاسِعٌ: ample in ruling, not easily invalidated or spoiled

ai.seo_question: When does well water become impure, and how is it purified again in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the purity of well water. It states that well water is not rendered impure by mere contact with impurity unless its smell or taste changes, and if that occurs, water is drawn out until the change disappears because the well has a replenishing source.
